facts.statement: Bruntonichthys is an extinct genus containing only one species of arthrodire placoderm.
facts.quote: Bruntonichthys is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm from the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.

facts.statement: The skull of Bruntonichthys was approximately 139 millimetres long and featured disproportionately large eye sockets.
facts.quote: The skull is about 139 millimetres long, and had disproportionally large eye sockets.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Bruntonichthys may have preyed on small mollusks.
facts.quote: Researchers suggest it may have preyed on small mollusks.

facts.statement: Fossils of Bruntonichthys have been found in the Gogo Formation in the Kimberley region of Australia.
facts.quote: Fossils are found in the Gogo Formation of the Kimberley region of Australia.

facts.statement: Bruntonichthys is a basal member of the clade Aspinothoracidi, which is part of the major clade Pachyosteomorphi within Eubrachythoraci.
facts.quote: Bruntonichthys is a basal member of the clade Aspinothoracidi, which belongs to the clade Pachyosteomorphi, one of the two major clades within Eubrachythoraci.

facts.statement: Bruntonichthys lived during the Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian, between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 372.15 million years ago)
